subject: SCIENCE
title: Homes That Meet Needs
introduction: A tadpole lives in a pond, and an earthworm lives in the soil. Why do these homes fit them so well?

vocabulary.definition: Everything around us — land, water, and air.
The place where a person or animal lives.
Something you must have to live, like food and water.

items.prompt: Which statement about environments is true?

options.text: Habitat is only a sleeping place
A suitable environment provides the particular resources and conditions an organism needs.

items.explanation: A good environment gives an animal what it needs — food, water, shelter, and space. One home does not suit every organism, and a habitat is more than a sleeping place.

items.prompt: Which example matches an organism to its environment?
items.explanation: Tadpoles need water, so a pond suits them. Fish cannot live in dry sand, and birds do not nest on bookshelves.

items.prompt: Which statement is not true?  (in this lesson: Homes That Meet Needs)
items.explanation: Different organisms need different homes, so one home cannot suit every organism. Some birds do live in tree canopies, and tadpoles do live in ponds.

items.prompt: Why might a pond suit a tadpole?

options.text: It provides water and resources it needs.

items.explanation: A pond gives a tadpole water and the resources it needs to grow. It is not made of paper, and not all animals can live there.
Earthworms need damp soil to live. Fish need water, and butterflies need air and flowers.
